name: Nostalgic flashback
desc: A better afternoon, remembered by someone who knows how it ended.

sets.place: sunlit classroom in summer, dust motes in the air, open window, white curtains

shots.desc: empty sunlit classroom, dust motes drifting in a shaft of light, open window, curtains moving, no humans
laughing, head tilted back, bright eyes, open smile, hair backlit by the window, close-up
white curtains lifting in a warm breeze, sunlight through the fabric, no humans
two empty desks pushed together by a window, initials carved into one lid, warm light, close-up, no humans

why: The tense is carried by the picture, not by a caption saying THEN. look:memory is the only grade in the library that softens as well as fades - contrast 0.92, saturation 0.60 and a gblur at sigma 1.4 - so a flashback is visibly a different image even in a single frame, and cue warm_memory is deliberately C major against a minor-key film, which reads as 'then' rather than 'now'. The sting is in the last shot: the desks are EMPTY, so the template ends by removing the person it just showed laughing. That is the shot that makes it nostalgia instead of simply a happy scene.
note: transition 'dissolve' is advisory - short.py renders hard cuts, which costs this template more than the others, since a dissolve is the conventional grammar for entering a memory. Until transitions land, sell the jump on the look change alone. Also important: wear 0 here is a request compile.py may refuse. wear is resolved as max() across movie, chapter and scene and is never allowed to decrease, so dropping this template into a film that has already reached wear 3 renders the flashback in torn, bloodied clothing. To use it late in a film, author it as its own chapter with wear reset at movie level, or accept the damage.
